answer: Twenty years of on-time payments cannot be typed into existence; they accumulate one month at a time, and Credit history depth simply reads that accumulation: a credit file with twenty years of on-time payments. The verifier never trusts a screenshot - it pulls the file from the bureau, and the tide is the file's own memory, twenty years deep. What breaks the farm is the voyage: a hundred aliases need a hundred such files, each with its own two decades, and the copper of buying them - if they were even for sale - would exceed every payout the epoch offers.
